steps: Represent the XOR carrier as H_N(x)=<A_N(x),Y_SAT> over F_2.
Try to prove C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} from the claim that A_N({0,1}^N) has no low-dimensional affine sketch.
Observe that any exact or approximate piecewise-affine sketch yields a small H_N circuit by hardwiring the SAT inner products of the affine bases.
Strengthen the necessary audit to piecewise-affine sketches with exceptional-set correction cost EN.
Test whether large rank alone suffices; it fails because the fixed SAT label vector may be simple on the generated image.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR Carrier Approximate Affine-Sketch Gate

assumptions: There is a circuit S_N of size s that, on input x, outputs a piece index t\in[K] and coordinates z\in\mathbb F_2^r.
For all but E exceptional inputs x, A_N(x)=a_t+\sum_{i\le r} z_i b_{t,i} over \mathbb F_2, where a_t,b_{t,i}\in\mathbb F_2^{U_L} are nonuniformly fixed for the carrier length.
Exceptional inputs are patched by equality gates of total size O(EN).
Circuit size is unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuit size for H_N.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=\bigoplus_{j\le M} SAT(G_{N,j}(x)), where M=N^q, each query has length L=(\log N)^d, and A_N(x)\in\mathbb F_2^{U_L} is the parity-incidence vector of generated formulas.
target object: SAT on L-bit instances, with intended consequence SAT\notin SIZE(n^c) for every fixed c, hence NP\not\subseteq P/poly if the carrier lower bound and transfer are both valid.
controlled interface: G_N has circuit size N^{\rho+o(1)} and SAT\in SIZE(n^c) substitutes into all M polylog-length queries with total size N^{\max\{\rho,q\}+o(1)}.
target-preserving condition: d>1 and \max\{\rho,q\}<1+\epsilon; source audits may hardwire constants only as upper-bound falsifiers and must not be advertised as target lower-bound evidence.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No nontrivial Fourier L1 upper bound exists for unrestricted polynomial-size circuits; the target threshold collapses before reaching P-vs-NP.
steps: Assume a proof establishes ||hat SAT_m||_1 > m^k or even > 2^{alpha m}.
Try to infer SAT_m notin SIZE(m^k) by treating small circuits as low spectral-norm objects.
The required target lemma would be: every size m^k circuit h has ||hat h||_1 <= B_SIZE(m,k) below the SAT threshold.
This target lemma is false: IP_r has O(m^2)-size circuits and ||hat IP_r||_1=2^{m/2}.
Restricting to L-leaf decision trees repairs the derivation because B_DT=L is true.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The work gives a valid restricted-model bridge and a falsifier for a route, not evidence for P != NP. A separate SAT-specific lower bound plus a true target compiler would still be needed.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: Fourier Spectral Norm Gate

assumptions: Fourier characters are over the uniform Boolean cube and functions are encoded as +/-1.
The target model C is fixed before the lower bound is interpreted.
No invariance under arbitrary many-one reductions is assumed.
definitions: source object: the +/-1 truth table f:{0,1}^m->{-1,1}, with intended source f=SAT_m and N=2^m truth-table length.
target object: deterministic decision trees with L leaves, or a named subclass C[m^k] such that every target function h has ||hat h||_1 <= B_C(m,k).
controlled interface: Walsh-Fourier L1 norm computed from the complete truth table; transfer uses only the inequality ||hat f||_1>B_C(m,k).
target-preserving condition: the threshold must be on the same m-bit slice, must exceed the named target upper bound, and must not be supplied by padding or an easy NP-complete carrier branch.

equations.label: spectral_norm
equations.valid_when: Valid when f is a +/-1 truth table on m Boolean inputs and Fourier characters use the uniform cube measure.

equations.label: decision_tree_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when h is computed by a deterministic decision tree with L leaves over the same m coordinates.

equations.label: inner_product_falsifier_norm

assumptions: N=2^m and construction time poly(N) is allowed in the natural-proof audit.
tau is below the random-function spectral norm scale.
The target class has an independently proved spectral-norm ceiling.

controlled interface: fast Walsh-Hadamard transform computes the certificate from the whole truth table.

assumptions: u has n bits, b is a tag bit, and v has 2r bits.
The IP branch is polynomial-time computable and has polynomial-size circuits.
SAT reduces to the b=0 slice by a length-controlled map.

target object: any route that treats high Fourier L1 norm of an NP-complete carrier as evidence about SAT_m.

target-preserving condition: the proof must localize the lower bound to the SAT slice or prove that reductions cannot inject an easy high-norm branch.

The spectral-norm certificate is a truth-table analytic property and supplies no nonrelativizing mechanism by itself. The decisive obstruction here is target-model collapse, not an oracle separation.
No algebraic-extension argument is being used. Any later algebraic Fourier proof must still identify a nonalgebrizing feature separately.
Many-one NP-completeness does not preserve Fourier L1 evidence; tagged easy branches can dominate the statistic while leaving SAT hardness unchanged.

Random truth tables give a large, poly(N)-constructive high-norm property; if claimed useful against full circuits it would be a natural proof, but usefulness fails because of IP_r.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No current construction gives a no-advice, low-D, E-canonical image family with a proof of diagonal anti-ball avoidance without either dense naturalness, brute-force enumeration, or subthreshold decoder leakage.
steps: Define U_m as the union, over all unrestricted circuits A of size at most 2^{xi m} and all max{xi,eta}<=epsilon-rho, of Hamming balls B(A,2^{eta m}).

The cover bound gives log_2|U_m|<=2^{(epsilon-rho)m+O(log m)}, so random truth tables avoid U_m with probability 1-o(1). Hence M=2^{D m} random rows are simultaneously anti-ball with overwhelming probability.
Try to choose the lexicographically first M rows outside U_m to obtain a canonical low-D carrier.
Testing whether a candidate row lies outside U_m requires enumerating threshold circuits, taking time 2^{2^{epsilon m+o(m)}}, so lex-first selection is not E-canonical.

Try to derandomize the random rows by a standard succinct PRG or local sampler. If its point-access exponent alpha is below epsilon-rho, each row has circuits of size 2^{alpha m+o(m)}, which is a falsifier for MCSP no-side soundness.
The only surviving source shape is a sparse no-advice sequential unranker with point-access exponent at least epsilon-rho, together with a non-large proof of diagonal anti-ball soundness.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge lemma is valid conditional route progress, but the source theorem is missing; it neither proves P != NP nor gives an unconditional explicit MCSP-hard row.

assumptions: Constants epsilon,rho,D are fixed with 0<rho<epsilon<1 and D>=0.
For each relevant m, I_m has at most 2^{D m+O(1)} distinct rows and admits bit computation T_i(x) in 2^{O(m)} time.
Source lengths are kappa-dense: every large target length n maps to an m with n<=kappa(1+D)m+O(1).
The anti-ball condition ranges over unrestricted Boolean circuits, not merely uniform or restricted circuit classes.
definitions: source object: a sequence of image families I_m subset {0,1}^{2^m} with distinct-image entropy D, canonical unranking in E time, and at least one row T in I_m satisfying AB_{epsilon,rho}.
target object: the padded multiplexed language L_I(i,x,pad)=T_i(x), where i indexes a canonical distinct image and x has length m.
controlled interface: MCSP-type anti-ball row witness -> E circuit lower bound via distinct-image multiplexing and kappa-balanced padding.

target-preserving condition: all indexing, length selection, and unranking are uniform without advice, and the source lengths are kappa-dense enough to transfer the lower bound to the declared target lengths.

equations.label: AB-diagonal
equations.valid_when: Valid when distances are between length-2^m truth tables and circuits are unrestricted Boolean circuits on m inputs.

equations.label: rooted-edit-upper-bound
equations.latex: \operatorname{dist}(T,A)\le 2^{\eta m}\ \wedge\ C(A)\le 2^{\xi m}\quad\Rightarrow\quad C(T)\le C(A)+O(m2^{\eta m})\le 2^{\max\{\xi,\eta\}m+o(m)}
equations.valid_when: Applies when T is obtained from A by explicitly hardwiring at most 2^{eta m} edited input points.

equations.label: multiplex-transfer
equations.valid_when: Requires the padding map and distinct-image multiplexing preserve uniformity without advice on every target length.

equations.label: forbidden-cover-size
equations.valid_when: Valid when xi and eta are fixed below one and circuits use a standard finite gate basis.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any row T in the source within 2^{eta m} edits of a size-2^{xi m} circuit with max{xi,eta}<epsilon-rho, since the rooted-edit upper bound then destroys MCSP no-side soundness.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Main repaired bridge for this cycle: it replaces rooted-volume heuristics by a diagonal anti-ball invariant and gives the exact transfer exponent.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A kappa-dense, E-canonical, low-distinct-image MCSP carrier with one row satisfying the diagonal anti-ball condition at exponent epsilon-rho yields a valid E-language unrestricted circuit lower bound with exponent any delta<(epsilon-rho)/(kappa(1+D)). This is a route bridge only, not P != NP.

assumptions: The construction is used as an external verifier over arbitrary truth tables, not merely as a sparse certificate for a named image family.
Circuit size is unrestricted nonuniform Boolean size.
The standard natural-proofs obstruction is treated as a route falsifier, not as an unconditional impossibility theorem.
definitions: dense predicate P_m: a predicate on N=2^m bit truth tables decidable in poly(N) time.
largeness: Pr_T[P_m(T)=1]>=N^{-O(1)} or any stronger noticeable density.
usefulness: P_m rejects every truth table computable by circuits of size 2^{(epsilon-rho)m}.
barrier status: dense constructive anti-ball is natural; sparse image certification is only outside the known natural-proofs scope, not automatically nonrelativizing or nonalgebrizing.

equations.label: random-density-of-antiball
equations.valid_when: Applies to uniformly random truth tables after the forbidden union is counted over all unrestricted circuits.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier audit: it separates a valid sparse carrier source from an invalid dense constructive hardness property.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the anti-ball certificate is upgraded to a polynomial-time truth-table predicate of noticeable density that rejects every subthreshold circuit, then the route has become a Razborov-Rudich natural-proof object. The carrier remains outside this barrier only while the accepted set is sparse, non-large, or not constructively decidable over all truth tables.

assumptions: Circuit encodings have O(S log S) bits for size S.
The verifier is not allowed nonuniform advice naming a hard row or a precomputed forbidden-union complement.
The target consequence is an E lower bound, not a higher-time lower bound.
definitions: enumerative verifier: a verifier that checks a candidate row against all circuits of the target size and all relevant edit balls.
E-canonical budget: bit unranking and certificate verification must run in 2^{O(m)} time to keep the multiplexed language in E.
threshold collapse: source certification time 2^{2^{Omega(m)}} cannot be hidden in the target-preserving interface.

equations.valid_when: Valid when a proposed certificate generator verifies anti-ball membership by explicit enumeration of all threshold circuits.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative obstruction for source construction; it explains why random anti-ball existence has not yet become a valid carrier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Brute-force certification of the diagonal anti-ball condition by enumerating all circuits up to size 2^{epsilon m} is not E-canonical. It proves combinatorial existence but cannot serve as the MCSP carrier interface.

Conditional transfer is valid with exponent delta<(epsilon-rho)/(kappa(1+D)) using distinct-image multiplexing and kappa-balanced padding.
Dense constructive anti-ball predicates are natural-proof objects; sparse carrier certificates remain only outside the known largeness condition.
Brute-force circuit enumeration proves existence but violates the E-canonical verifier and unranking budget.
Point-access exponent alpha<epsilon-rho gives small circuits for rows; alpha>=epsilon-rho is necessary for a valid source.

falsifier: the anti-ball certificate is a dense poly(N)-time predicate over all truth tables, making the route a natural-proof object rather than a sparse carrier.
falsifier: the unranker or decoder computes T_i(x) with point-access exponent alpha<epsilon-rho, yielding small circuits for every row.
falsifier: source soundness is justified only by enumerating all size-2^{epsilon m} circuits, exceeding the 2^{O(m)} E-canonical interface.
falsifier: a nonuniform selector or advice string names the hard row or the source length, so the target lower bound is only nonuniform leakage.
falsifier: the source exists only infinitely often without kappa-dense padding, giving at best an i.o. target and not the claimed all-length transfer.
